pr_title: Add support for Shelly RPC devices custom TCP port
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add TCP custom port support for Shelly devices.

Shelly devices that support such feature, can now be used as "range extender".
On top, Shelly Gen2/Gen3 devices behind a NAT can be configured in Home Assistant as well.

**NOTE**: Shelly range extender doesn't support CoAP port forwarding, thus Gen1 devices cannot be configured with custom ports.

issue_context.title: Shelly Integration: Unable to Parse Address with a Port
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello. I appreciate the development and support.

I found an issue with the built-in Shelly integration.

I have two Shelly Pro 3 EMs (I believe generation 2?) running the latest stable firmware (1.1.0). They live on a different subnet from my HA server (2024.1.5) and have a static IP addresses. Only HTTP (over a nonstandard port) is forwarded to the Shellys.

Following the instructions at https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/ for gen 2/3 devices, I enabled outbound WebSocket and entered the HA address (ws://IP:PORT/api/shelly/ws).

When I try Add Integration to connect to the Shelly (IP:PORT), I get an “Unexpected Error”. In the logs, this looks like the port is not being handled properly: “ValueError: ‘IP:PORT’ does not appear to be an IPv4 or IPv6 address”.

If I forward port 80 to the Shelly, I can connect and add a device and entities, but I have only one port 80 on the firewall and multiple Shellys.

It seems like the integration does not parse an address with a port properly.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Shelly

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Unexpected exception

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/aioshelly/common.py", line 68, in process_ip_or_options
    ipaddress.ip_address(options.ip_address)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/ipaddress.py", line 54, in ip_address
    raise ValueError(f'{address!r} does not appear to be an IPv4 or IPv6 address')
ValueError: 'IP:PORT' does not appear to be an IPv4 or IPv6 address

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/shelly/config_flow.py", line 142, in async_step_user
    device_info = await validate_input(
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/shelly/config_flow.py", line 76, in validate_input
    rpc_device = await RpcDevice.create(
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/aioshelly/rpc_device/device.py", line 95, in create
    options = await process_ip_or_options(ip_or_options)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/aioshelly/common.py", line 71, in process_ip_or_options
    options.ip_address = await loop.run_in_executor(
                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
socket.gaierror: [Errno -2] Name does not resolve
```

> Following the instructions at https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/ for gen 2/3 devices, I enabled outbound WebSocket and entered the HA address (ws://IP:PORT/api/shelly/ws).

Only battery powered devices require an outbound websocket to be enabled.

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/478555/615d5d79-72c3-4133-8afd-a1d5a5bcb2da)

When configuring your Shelly device, you only need to provide an IP address or hostname.

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/478555/7d102b7f-5e3b-46ff-bd77-77e4ece27ba1)

Sorry for the misunderstanding; there are multiple Shellys behind a single IP address (NAT), so a port must be specified. The configuration is able to connect with the non-standard port specified (separated by the colon delimiter), as it asks for the password, but is not able to complete the integration setup. From the log, it seems like it doesn't know what to do with the port later in the setup.

(I will disable the Outbound WebSocket, since you advise that that is not necessary.)

> there are multiple Shellys behind a single IP address (NAT), so a port must be specified.

Such configuration is not supported.

Oh, that's surprising, especially since the integration accepts the input and successfully connects (to the point of asking for a password).

I would think that this (segmented networks) is not an uncommon scenario.

All other integrations that I have used thus far (admittedly, I am fairly new to this and the sample size is not large) have some provision for non-standard ports when applicable. This is sometimes in the form of entering IP:PORT (as here) and sometimes as a separate field that is pre-filled with the default.

Could the devs of this integration please complete the support for non-standard ports?

Thank you.

review_comments: We could also hide this behind `self.show_advanced_options` so it would only be seen if the user has advanced enabled
